message.abstract: <jats:p>The classification of mushroom cultures has traditionally depended on manual evaluation performed by trained experts. Although widely used, this approach is vulnerable to subjective judgment, human bias, and observational errors. To address these shortcomings, this study proposes an automated classification framework based on machine learning techniques. Two different approaches are implemented: the first utilizes histogram analysis in the HSV color space, while the second applies a convolutional neural network (CNN)–based model. The proposed system was evaluated using a dataset comprising 1400 images of Pleurotus ostreatus mycelium collected from two different strains over a cultivation period of 14 days. During growth analysis, histogram profiles were generated from masked regions of interest. The HSV histogram method achieved an average precision of 74.6% during Phase 2, which increased to 95.2% in Phase 3. In the CNN-based approach, distinctive image features were automatically extracted from rhizomorph mycelium growth images and used to train predictive models. The developed MNet and MConNet architectures attained an average accuracy of 92.15% for growth-stage prediction and 97.81% for contamination detection. The experimental results demonstrate that computer vision–based machine learning systems have strong potential to enhance mushroom cultivation by improving reliability, reducing dependence on manual inspection, and increasing overall productivity and crop quality.</jats:p>
title: AUTOMATING MUSHROOM CULTURE CLASSIFICATION: A MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH
